sentences: The council of the fictional coastal town of Westmere approved a plan on Tuesday to rebuild its harbour wall.
The wall was badly damaged during two winter storms last year.
Engineers estimate that the work will take eighteen months.
Local fishing crews have welcomed the decision after months of uncertainty.
The project will be funded through a mix of regional grants and a new mooring fee.
Councillors said the fee would apply only to visiting leisure boats.
Some residents argued that the town should have applied for national funding instead.
The finance committee will publish a detailed budget next month.
Construction is expected to disrupt traffic on the seafront road.
A temporary one-way system will run from March until the end of the summer season.
Businesses on the promenade have asked for extra signage to guide visitors to car parks.
A new public library opened its doors in the centre of the fictional city of Brackley on Saturday.
More than two thousand visitors came through the entrance on the first day.
The building replaces a smaller branch that closed five years ago.
The library includes a makerspace with 3D printers and a recording studio.
Staff will run free weekly workshops for teenagers on coding and podcast production.
Organisers hope the space will attract young people who rarely visit libraries.
The opening comes as many libraries across the region face reduced budgets.
Campaigners say that local branches are often the only free indoor space left in a neighbourhood.
The city plans to review opening hours at its other branches later this year.
Officials have not ruled out further closures.
Thousands of runners took part in the annual Northfield marathon on Sunday under clear skies.
The winner finished the course in two hours and eleven minutes.
It was the fastest time recorded in the history of the event.
Organisers introduced reusable cups at every water station this year.
They estimate that the change prevented around forty thousand plastic cups from being thrown away.
Volunteers collected the cups at the finish line for washing.
The race raised money for a children's hospital and a mental health charity.
Early figures suggest that participants collected more than half a million pounds.
The final total will be announced at a ceremony next month.
